evidenceCoverage.coverageCaveat: Every direct verification attempt this run — the target site itself, an archived snapshot, and all five registers listed above — was blocked or unreachable. Nothing in this brief is based on a directly loaded primary page or register record; all findings rest on secondary web-search reporting. In particular: no register was reached that could confirm or deny an Argentine licence for this domain (authorisation stays null, not a confirmed 'not found'); no registration data (registrar, creation date, registrant) could be obtained; and no operator entity could be identified. The comparatively stronger actorBehaviour evidence (a documented Betsson-brand mirror-domain evasion episode in Chile) is real and independently sourced, but is not itself evidence about this specific domain's content or targeting of Argentina.

executiveSummary.headline: betsson1002.com could not be directly investigated — the target site, domain-registration registers, and legal-entity registers were all blocked at the network-egress level this run — but secondary reporting shows the site self-presents under the "Betsson" brand on a domain outside Argentina's mandatory '.bet.ar' licensed-operator naming convention, and the same brand name was tied to a documented mirror-domain evasion episode in Chile days earlier.
executiveSummary.narrative: betsson1002.com was submitted as a suspected illegal gambling site targeting Argentina via an internal watchlist item, not itself a public-source finding. Direct fetch of the target (https and http, with and without the www prefix), an archived snapshot via the Wayback Machine, the IANA RDAP bootstrap file, the .com registry's RDAP endpoint (rdap.verisign.com), the GLEIF LEI API, a WHOIS/domain-keyword aggregator (whoxy.com), Argentina's CABA gambling regulator LOTBA's own site, and two secondary-press pages were all blocked or unreachable from the investigating environment, so no finding below rests on a directly loaded primary register or on the target's own page content. What is known comes entirely from search-engine indexing and independent press reporting. A web-search index snippet titles the page "Betsson: Online Casino, Live Casino & Sportsbetting", i.e. the site self-presents using the well-known Betsson brand name; however betsson1002.com does not match any of Betsson's known official domains (betsson.com, betsson.co, betsson.lt, betssonab.com), nor does it use the '.bet.ar' domain that multiple independent Argentine sources report is mandatory for provincially-licensed online gambling operators (Betsson itself holds active licences from LOTBA, IPLyC-PBA and the Cordoba lottery, and operates in Argentina under a .bet.ar domain per those sources). Argentine authorities blocked several hundred unauthorized gambling domains during 2026 (500+ in a July operation, 251 in an earlier one), underscoring that non-'.bet.ar' domains are treated as unlicensed at scale. Separately, and independently of the Argentine context, multiple Chilean outlets (Diario Financiero, Emol, Chócale, La Cuarta) reported that Chile's telecoms regulator Subtel ordered 42 gambling domains blocked on 2026-09-01, that a domain associated with the Betsson brand was on that list, and that several of the listed operators activated new domains within 24–48 hours to keep operating — a documented, brand-linked mirror-domain evasion pattern. No source reviewed this run specifically named betsson1002.com as the replacement domain used in that Chilean episode; one search-engine summary asserted that link, but the underlying article could not be loaded to confirm it (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so that specific attribution is treated as unverified and is not relied upon as a finding.

Multiple independent Chilean press sources confirm that a domain associated with the Betsson brand was targeted by a Chilean Subtel blocking order on 2026-09-01, and that Betsson-branded and other operators on that list activated replacement domains within 24–48 hours — a verified, brand-linked mirror-domain evasion pattern, though no source confirmed betsson1002.com itself as that specific replacement domain.

Argentina blocked 500+ (July 2026) and 251 (earlier 2026) unauthorized online-gambling domains at scale, and CABA regulator LOTBA is separately reported to have acted against unauthorized sites and promoting influencers — general market/enforcement context, not evidence specific to this domain.

No operator entity, registration data, or licence claim could be established for betsson1002.com from any source reached this run; legal entity, parent group, and domain-registration fields are all null.

Argentina has active, working mechanisms for blocking unauthorized gambling domains at scale (500+ domains blocked July 2026 in Buenos Aires Province; 251 blocked via an earlier Enacom/judicial order), suggesting a referral for this single domain would be procedurally straightforward if pursued through the same channel. Collateral-risk factors such as shared hosting or CDN use could not be assessed since RDAP/hosting data was blocked.

A confirmed case of unauthorized impersonation of a brand ('Betsson') that itself holds legitimate Argentine provincial licences would carry consumer-protection messaging value, but this domain's operator identity and affiliation are not yet established, limiting certainty of that framing.

analystNotes: This case rested almost entirely on secondary web-search reporting because the target site and every register attempted (RDAP bootstrap, .com registry RDAP, GLEIF, a WHOIS aggregator, and Argentina's own LOTBA register) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. Two points warrant analyst attention on re-run. First, a search-engine summary asserted that betsson1002.com was specifically the domain Betsson activated in Chile after the 2026-09-01 Subtel blocking order; the primary article could not be loaded to confirm this, so it is treated as an unverified inference by the search layer, not a finding, and is flagged rather than relied upon — worth re-checking directly once epicentrochile.com or an equivalent source is reachable. Second, the naming pattern (a well-known gambling brand name plus a numeric suffix, on a generic .com TLD rather than Argentina's mandatory '.bet.ar') is the kind of pattern associated with brand-impersonation mirror domains, but this is inference from naming convention and indexed metadata only — nothing about this domain's actual content, operator, or hosting was directly observed this run.
